chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The boundary of Al-Rawdah is from the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) to the edge of Al-Zhialal, and the boundary of the Mosque is to the two pillars on the right of the pulpit to the road from the side facing the Night Market."

key_terms.اَلرَّوْضَة: Al-Rawdah (The Garden/Precinct), a sacred area adjacent to the Prophet's Mosque.
key_terms.اَلظِّلاَل: Al-Zhialal, a specific landmark or area mentioned in classical texts.
key_terms.اَلْأُسْطُوَتَان: The two pillars, structural landmarks within the mosque.
key_terms.اَلْمِنْبَر: The pulpit, located within the mosque.
key_terms.سُوقُ اَللَّيْل: The Night Market, a historical market in Medina.
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ اَلرَّسُول: The Mosque of the Messenger (Prophet's Mosque).

ai.seo_question: What are the defined boundaries of Al-Rawdah and the Mosque in Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq delineates the sacred precincts of Medina by distinguishing between the broader Al-Rawdah (extending to the Night Market) and the inner Masjid proper (bounded by the two pillars), a distinction crucial for understanding the legal status of these areas in Shia jurisprudence. This narration provides the foundational geographical markers used by scholars to determine the sanctity and specific rulings, such as prayer validity and prohibition of impurities, associated with the Prophet's burial place.
